post.caption: Idar-Oberstein's cutters worked lying down. Idar-Oberstein is a German town famous for cutting gems. Local agate finds were first mentioned in the 1370s. Rivers turned sandstone wheels that ground the agate. Cutters lay on tilted wooden benches facing the wheel. A water wheel mill from 1754 ran until 1945. Local emigrants found huge agate deposits in Brazil in the 1820s. The first Brazilian shipment reached Idar in 1834 and started a boom. Brazil also sent amethyst and other colored stones. That made the town a center for colored stones. Visitors can walk about 400 meters of the Steinkaulenberg gem mine.
